name: Buckhorn Bar Campground
note: 9 single sites plus 4 walk-in tent sites along the South Fork Salmon River, Krassel RD, Payette NF; tables/fire rings/grills, vault toilets, drinking water, no hookups. First-come, first-served (Scan & Pay). --Claude

name: Last Chance Campground
note: 20 single + 3 double sites along the west bank of Goose Creek, 2.2 mi up Last Chance Rd (FR 453) north of McCall, New Meadows RD, Payette NF; extended spurs for longer RVs, potable water (summer), vault toilets, camp host May-Sept, no hookups; Goose Creek Trail #533 starts here. First-come, first-served (Scan & Pay). --Claude

name: Ponderosa Campground
note: Payette NF campground on the Secesh River near Yellow Pine; ~10 primitive drive-in sites, drinking water, vault toilets, no hookups. First-come, first-served (not on recreation.gov for booking). Reached via Lick Creek Rd (FR 48) / Yellow Pine gravel roads. --Claude

name: Grouse Campground
note: Payette NF campground on Goose Lake, ~16 mi from McCall via Goose Lake Rd/FR 257 (paved then ~10 mi gravel); 21 sites with drinking water, vault toilets and a boat ramp, no hookups; sites take RVs/trailers ~20-45 ft. Reservable online, some FCFS. --Claude

name: Upper Payette Lake Campground
note: Payette NF campground on Upper Payette Lake, ~16 mi N of McCall via Warren Wagon Rd; 32 sites (listed to 30-78 ft), drinking water, vault toilets, boat ramp and a paved shoreline trail, no hookups. ~8 reservable + ~12 first-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Hazard Lake Campground
note: High alpine (~7,100 ft) Payette NF campground beside Hazard Lake, ~18 mi gravel (Goose Lake Rd/FR 257) NW of Brundage Mtn; 12 primitive sites, drinking water (Jul-Sep), vault toilets, no hookups. Best for tents and small RVs; larger trailers not recommended. First-come, first-served (scan-and-pay). --Claude

name: Ebenezer Campground
note: Primitive Salmon-Challis NF campground on the Wild & Scenic Salmon River along Salmon River Rd (FR 030) W of North Fork. 11 non-hookup sites, picnic tables, fire pits, vault toilet, drinking water. First-come, first-served, self-pay (cash). Elev ~3,140 ft. --Claude

name: Twin Creek Campground
note: USFS (Salmon-Challis NF, North Fork RD) campground on Twin Creek near its confluence with the North Fork Salmon, 15 mi north of North Fork on US-93 then 0.5 mi on FR 156. 37 single-family drive-in sites (first-come, first-served) plus 1 reservable group site; tables, fire rings, drinking water, vault toilets, no hookups; accommodates trailers and RVs. Group site reservable online mid-May through Labor Day. --Claude

name: Red River Campground
note: USFS campground (Nez Perce-Clearwater NF) along the Red River on Red River Hot Springs Rd #234, ~4 mi east of the closed Red River Ranger Station. Sites with picnic tables and metal fire rings, vault toilets, potable water; first-come, first-served (not on recreation.gov). Large RVs have limited access — larger rigs should preview the site before entering. --Claude

name: French Gulch Campground
note: Small USFS campground on the Red River Ranger District, Nez Perce-Clearwater NF. 2 sites with vault toilet; no potable water, first-come, first-served (pack-in/pack-out). Reached via gravel Red River-Dixie Rd #222 ~11 mi south of State Hwy 14. French Gulch Creek runs through camp; public fishing access on nearby Red River. Elev ~4,210 ft. --Claude

name: Crooked River Campground
note: Small USFS drive-in campgrounds on the Crooked River, Red River Ranger District, Nez Perce-Clearwater NF (Crooked River #3 = 1 pad, well-screened; #4 = 4 pads with a small fishing/swimming pond). Vault toilets; no potable water, first-come, first-served. Gravel access off Hwy 14 up the Crooked River Rd. --Claude

name: Leggett Creek Campground
note: USFS campground on the Red River Ranger District, Nez Perce-Clearwater NF, ~14 mi west of Elk City along State Hwy 14. 5 natural-surface sites with metal fire rings and one vault toilet; explicitly noted as accommodating larger RVs/trailers. No potable water, first-come, first-served. Public fishing access to Leggett Creek and the South Fork Clearwater River. --Claude

name: South Fork Campground
note: USFS campground along the South Fork Clearwater River at ~milepost 15 on State Hwy 14, Nez Perce-Clearwater NF. 9 sites, each with picnic table, grill, tent pad and paved parking spur; site #3 is 31 ft and #8 is 25 ft (others shorter). Vault toilets; drinking water in peak season; $12/night. Standard sites are first-come, first-served (a separate 25-person group site is reservable online). --Claude

name: Fish Creek Campground
note: USFS campground ~8 mi south of Grangeville on Forest Rd 221, Salmon River Ranger District, Nez Perce-Clearwater NF; 4-season recreation area (Fish Creek XC/OHV trail). 10 sites for tents and RVs, potable water, paved parking, camp host in peak season; individual sites first-come, first-served (the Fish Creek pavilion/group site is separately reservable). Elev ~5,100 ft. --Claude

name: Newsome Campground
note: Small primitive USFS campground on the Red River Ranger District, Nez Perce-Clearwater NF, near the historic Newsome Work Center; reached via gravel Newsome Creek Rd #1858 ~5.2 mi north of State Hwy 14. Fire rings, picnic table and vault toilet; no potable water, first-come, first-served; vehicles to ~24 ft. Fishing on Newsome and Beaver creeks; popular with hunters/ATV users. Elev ~4,000 ft. --Claude

name: Selway Falls Campground
note: USFS (Moose Creek RD, Nez Perce-Clearwater NF), 7 sites along Meadow Creek near its confluence with the Selway River at Selway Falls; vault toilet, no potable water; accommodates RVs under 30 ft. First-come, first-served, self-pay (May-Oct); access via gravel FR 223 (FS rates access difficult). NOTE: closed for the 2026 season due to fire impacts. --Claude

name: Rackliff Campground
note: USFS campground (Nez Perce-Clearwater NF) on the Selway River, ~9 mi SE of US-12 on FR 223 (Selway Rd), split by Rackliff Creek with a footbridge. 6 tent/RV sites, vault toilet, no potable water. First-come, first-served (May 12-Sep 30). --Claude

name: Johnson Bar Campground & Group Site
note: USFS campground (Nez Perce-Clearwater NF) on the Selway River, 4.5 mi E of Lowell on FR 223 (Selway Rd), set in a large open field on a river bar with a swimming beach. 7 individual RV/trailer-pad sites (first-come, first-served, $8) plus one reservable group site for up to 100 people ($40, May 12-Sep 30). Vault toilet. --Claude

name: Wild Goose Campground
note: Small USFS campground (Nez Perce-Clearwater NF) on the Middle Fork Clearwater River at milepost 98 on US-12 near Lowell. 8 sites, gravel parking, two vault toilets, no potable water; accommodates RVs to 24 ft. First-come, first-served (May 12-Sep 26), max 8 people per site. --Claude

name: Wilderness Gateway Campground
note: Large Nez Perce-Clearwater NF campground on the Wild & Scenic Lochsa River at US-12 milepost 122.5 (~2,100 ft); 89-91 single-family sites in multiple loops plus a large-group site and horse/stock facilities. Tables, fire rings, flush and vault toilets, drinking water. Most sites reservable online, some first-come, first-served. RVs and horse trailers accommodated. --Claude

name: Colgate Campground
note: Small primitive Forest Service overflow campground (Nez Perce-Clearwater NF) on the Lochsa River off US-12 near milepost 147; 7 first-come, first-served sites, vault toilet, no water. Some sites have river access down a steep bank. Small sites best for smaller rigs; near Colgate Licks and area hot springs. --Claude

name: Jerry Johnson Campground
note: Nez Perce-Clearwater NF campground along US-12 (~53 mi east of Lowell) across from the Wild & Scenic Lochsa River, near the popular Jerry Johnson Hot Springs trailhead; 20 first-come, first-served sites, tables, fire rings, vault toilets, potable water currently unavailable. Season ~June-October. --Claude

name: Whitehouse Campground
note: Nez Perce-Clearwater NF campground along the Lochsa River at US-12 milepost 158.5 (~4 mi west of Powell, ~3,337 ft); 13 sites accommodating RVs up to 30 ft, first-come, first-served. Damaged in the 2024 windstorm and closed for cleanup; restoration underway for reopening (per Idaho Fish & Game / USFS Good Neighbor Authority) — confirm current status before a trip. --Claude

name: Wendover Campground
note: Nez Perce-Clearwater NF campground in mature pine along the Wild & Scenic Lochsa River at US-12 milepost 158.2 (~4 mi west of Powell), centered on a small stream; 27 sites accommodating RVs up to 40 ft, first-come, first-served. Closed after the 2024 windstorm; restored and reopened June 2026 per Idaho Fish & Game / USFS. --Claude

name: Dam View Campground
note: USACE (Walla Walla District) campground overlooking Dworshak Dam/Reservoir near Ahsahka. Primitive dry camping, first-come first-served (no reservations); paved level RV/tent sites described big-rig friendly, potable water pump and vault/porta toilet, no hookups. --Claude

name: Weitas Creek Campground
note: Small USFS (Nez Perce-Clearwater NF, North Fork RD) campground on FSR 250 ~35 mi NE of Pierce, along Weitas Creek near its confluence with the North Fork Clearwater River. 6 primitive sites, first-come first-served; vault/portable toilet, no potable water, pack-in/pack-out. --Claude

name: Noe Creek Campground
note: Small USFS (Nez Perce-Clearwater NF, North Fork RD) campground on FSR 250 ~41 mi east of Pierce, in fir/larch with views of the North Fork Clearwater River. 6 units, small nightly fee, first-come first-served; outhouse, no potable water. Open ~May-Oct. --Claude

name: Washington Creek Campground
note: USFS (Nez Perce-Clearwater NF, North Fork RD) riverside campground on the banks of the North Fork Clearwater River, reached by a bridge off FSR 250. 23 sites (incl 1 group) plus host; gravel pads, picnic tables, fire rings, vault toilets, potable water spigots. First-come first-served, open ~May-Oct. --Claude

name: Kelly Forks Campground
note: USFS (Nez Perce-Clearwater NF, North Fork RD) campground at the confluence of Kelly Creek and the North Fork Clearwater River, on FSR 250. 14 sites plus a group area and host; RV access (no hookups), pit toilets, potable water, fire rings, tables. First-come first-served, open ~May-Oct. --Claude

name: Flat Creek Campground
note: Small primitive USFS (Nez Perce-Clearwater NF, North Fork RD) campground on FSR 250 along the North Fork Clearwater River, between Washington Creek and Kelly Forks. About 6 sites, first-come first-served, primitive (no potable water); bring your own supplies. --Claude

name: Elk Creek Campground
note: USFS (Nez Perce-Clearwater NF) campground on Elk Creek in a mature pine forest <1 mi from the town of Elk River (~3,000 ft). Single-family tent/RV sites with electrical hookups; most FCFS, 6 sites reservable online (up to 4 days ahead). Near Elk Creek Reservoir and Elk Creek Falls. --Claude

name: Cedars Campground
note: Small primitive USFS campground (5 sites) at the confluence of Long Creek and the North Fork Clearwater River (Nez Perce-Clearwater NF); first-come first-served, vault toilets, no potable water — pack it in/out. Access via rough, washboard, narrow forest road; a 25-ft Class C reportedly fit but large Class A rigs not advised. --Claude

name: Laird Park Campground
note: USFS Nez Perce-Clearwater CG on the Palouse River (Palouse Ranger District, near Harvard/Potlatch); 31 single sites plus a group site, max camper 30 ft, vault toilets, CCC-built dammed swimming beach, first-come first-served. Potable water not available in 2026. --Claude

name: Spruce Tree Campground
note: USFS Idaho Panhandle CG on the St. Joe River at the start of its Wild & Scenic section (St. Joe Ranger District), 12 mi up Red Ives Rd #218 from the St. Joe River Rd; 9 units, vault toilets, hand-pump potable water (roughly Jun-Sep), first-come first-served. Access road paved much of the way then narrow single-lane gravel with few turnouts; some sites fit 30+ ft and there is one pull-through. --Claude

name: Cedar Creek Campground
note: Small USFS Idaho Panhandle CG (3 sites) directly off State Hwy 3 about 3 mi north of Clarkia, on the St. Maries River (St. Joe Ranger District); vault toilet, no potable water (pack in/out), first-come first-served. --Claude

name: Mammoth Springs Campground
note: USFS Idaho Panhandle CG (8 units) high on the St. Joe/Clearwater divide near Avery, ~5,650 ft (St. Joe Ranger District); vault toilets, potable water mid-Jul-Sep, first-come first-served. A popular hunting/OHV base camp reached by rough forest roads (Bluff Creek Rd #509 + Avery-Timber Creek Rd #201) — high clearance advised, but Campendium reports a 40-ft rig has camped here. --Claude

name: Shadowy St. Joe Campground
note: USFS (St. Joe RD, Idaho Panhandle NF), on the St. Joe River 10.6 mi from St. Maries on FH 50. Fully rebuilt 2023 (Great American Outdoors Act + IDPR RV grant): electric hookups at all 14 sites, new restrooms, boat launch/docks, group picnic shelter; slack-water river. ~7 sites reservable in peak season, rest FCFS. --Claude

name: Bumblebee Campground
note: Idaho Panhandle NF (Coeur d'Alene River RD) campground where Bumblebee Creek meets the Little North Fork Coeur d'Alene River, ~2,200 ft. Two loops, 23 single sites plus a large group site; paved/chip-sealed roads and parking areas take rigs up to ~80 ft. Hand-pump drinking water at the group site, vault toilets, no hookups. About half the sites are reservable online, the rest first-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Kit Price Campground
note: Idaho Panhandle NF (Coeur d'Alene River RD) campground along the North Fork Coeur d'Alene River. Three loops, ~57-58 nonelectric sites including 7 doubles and 10 pull-throughs, RVs/trailers to 40 ft; fully renovated in 2021 (new paved spurs, tables, fire rings, restrooms), drinking water, vault toilets, no hookups. Both first-come, first-served and reservable sites (reservable online). Popular for river swimming, tubing and float trips. --Claude

name: Devil's Elbow Campground
note: Idaho Panhandle NF (Coeur d'Alene River RD) campground on the banks of the North Fork Coeur d'Alene River, ~2,600 ft, in lodgepole/mixed pine. 20 sites including a host site and a group site (to 50 people); roads paved, parking spurs short but wide (best for mid-size rigs — check per-site length), hand-pump drinking water, vault toilets, no hookups. Both first-come, first-served and reservable sites (reservable online). River rafting, kayaking and catch-and-release cutthroat fishing. --Claude
